subject: Re: Seedling Energy - advance commit options for 3-year engagement
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@seedling.energy>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@seedling.energy
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: 3-year advance-commit options and preferred economics

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers and the cost profile. We're preparing our budget for the next three fiscal years and would like to evaluate a 3-year advance commit with Redwood.

High-level ask: can you share (a) a simple upfront prepay option with a single blended discount for a full 3-year, and (b) a stepped/ramped schedule (lower Y1, increasing discount in Y2/Y3) that includes a true-up at each anniversary? Our finance team prefers an advance-payment structure but needs some protection if our usage under-indexes.

Rough sizing: we expect ~400k tokens/month in year 1, conservative growth to ~1.1M tokens/month by year 3. We can provide monthly usage reports and agree to annual true-ups.

Timeline: procurement would like a term sheet and indicative pricing by end of week so they can start legal review.

Appreciate any options and the mechanics (true-up, clawbacks, invoice timing, DocuSign flow).

Alex
VP Product
Seedling Energy

Attachments: none referenced
From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: 3-year advance-commit options and preferred economics

Alex — thanks for the clear sizing. Below are two clean structures we can table quickly; I've looped in Marissa from Finance to validate the billing mechanics and DocuSign path.

Option A — 3-year Accelerator (single upfront payment)
- Upfront prepay covering estimated term usage (annualized) with an 18% blended discount off list rates if paid fully upfront.
- Annual true-up: if actual usage > prepay amount, incremental consumption billed at list less 5% (yearly true-up invoice). If actual usage < prepay amount, credits carry forward for up to 12 months; remaining credit is refundable at contract exit at prorated value (less a 2% early-exit admin fee).

Option B — StepRamp (annual invoiced, prefunded reserve + true-up)
- Year 1: 12% discount applied to committed bucket (billed at start of Y1).
- Year 2: 15% discount on the Year 2 committed bucket, Year 3: 20% discount.
- Each year has an annual true-up with a 60-day window. Underspend carries forward but expires at the end of year 3.
- We can include a limited under-usage protection: if Y1 usage < 60% of forecast, we will allow a one-time 50% refund of Y1 overpayment (capped).

Mechanics and asks from our side:
- We need a signed SOW and DocuSign envelope to lock the prepay.
- Finance will require a billing contact and bank remit details; prepay invoices are due within 30 days of signature.
- For the Accelerator model we usually require a small reserve (5% of total) to be retained for usage spikes.

If either option looks promising I can produce a short term sheet for procurement and route to legal. Do you have any flexibility on the blended prepay amount (we typically base it on 12x–18x your monthly run rate depending on growth confidence)?

Cheers,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Naomi — quick finance note so we can move to a signed term sheet: 

- Accelerator (18%): Finance is comfortable provisionally if Seedling pays the full upfront and we record it as deferred revenue. We will need a short cap on refund liability — recommend the 2% admin fee Naomi proposed.
- StepRamp: acceptable but requires confirmed payment schedule and an SLA credit cap if they request latency/uptime SLAs in contract.

Approvals/limits: I can approve up to a 16% blended discount without escalation. Anything >16% or structural exceptions (refund window >12 months, special escrow terms) must get finance leadership approval (Vivek).

Please include: forecasted monthly token schedule by month for the first 12 months and the entity/legal name they will sign under. Also confirm whether Seedling requires an amortization schedule for ASC 606.

Marissa Cole
Senior Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RE: Seedling Energy - advance commit options and preferred economics

Thanks for the write-up. I reviewed the numbers — this is a strategic vertical for us and Seedling is a strong reference if the implementation goes well. I'm ok approving a final Accelerator structure at 17% (one point below Naomi's 18%) on the condition that: 

1) We keep the 2% early-exit admin fee and a 12-month credit carry-forward cap.
2) Include a modest SLA credit schedule (max exposure 1.5% of ARR) tied to latency SLOs rather than unlimited credits.
3) Seedling signs within 30 days of receiving the term sheet and wire within 30 days of signature; otherwise the discount reverts to our standard 12% 3-year upfront.

If Seedling prefers the StepRamp, we can approve the Year 1 / Year 2 / Year 3 schedule Naomi suggested, but I want a 14% floor (i.e., any blended discount below 14% is not acceptable).

Rishi — loop you for commercial messaging and to confirm whether we should offer a 0.5% marketing credit for a case study.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Revenue and Partnerships
Redwood Inference
